items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: I had Otto Langs. I never forget his trumpet method.

ctx.x: He taught me too. Oh, yeah?

Yeah? Well, that's the man that really caught over my eyes about the music, see, because Henry Red Allen, he'd get over there and he'd be teaching me something. I kept my little book, you know, I had Otto Langs. I never forget his trumpet method. And Henry, he'd teach me a little something in there, and then he'd know that I liked the blow show, and then he'd put on a little records. He'd get there with his trumpet. And I'd get mine. Oh, yeah, he was like Dipper. And me and him would copy records. Well, I didn't…

You know, P. Ron used to tell Arthur Durbny, Leo Dejan when he was playing on the boat with Dirty Pope, he used to tell them, say, man, why don't you put that music on the side? Try to memorize the music. Yeah. He was just looking at the music all the time. I suppose the lights go out. Yeah, that's right. And you know what happened? You see? And we was in the middle of a tune.
